user_decision.question: Route S-2's first requirement is not dischargeable as filed: the iterated splice's interior REGISTER clause is refuted by compiled theorem, and with it Phase 11.20's ~_d relation, whose n = n' conjunct the pump's own position pairs do not satisfy. The countdown half of the same requirement is landed. How should the register coordinate be handled?
options: (W-1) Register-closed blocks: strengthen the type pigeonhole to sample a bounded register observable alongside (objAt, tpOf), so a pumped block satisfies nxtAt g u = nxtAt g (u + l) and the periodic extension of the original's register IS Drift-compatible at every copy boundary. This makes the refuted clause true under the strengthened block, at the cost of a new design question -- the register is unbounded in a pending-forever region, so the observable must be chosen and its own room charged against Tc.

(W-2) Weaken the invariant's register conjunct: replace ~_d's n = n' by whatever the pump's pairs actually satisfy (a Drift-distance bound, or a clipped/residue reading of the register), and re-derive the transport on that. Phase 11.21 already exists to bridge ~_d to the kappa-collision the consumer needs, so this moves the register bridging one phase earlier and re-opens Phase 11.20's pinned relation.

(W-3) Block the realization record whole on the register coordinate, landing the obstruction as the finding of record (the two compiled theorems are already landed) and stopping the depth-induction line here.
user_decision.recommendation: (W-2). The refutation shows the pump cannot hold the register, so (W-1) asks the pigeonhole to buy a property the construction destroys and then rebuilds -- a second design round with its own room budget, and the round-15 evidence already charges Tc once for the margin. (W-2) accepts the pump as it is and moves the register bridging into the invariant, which is where Phase 11.21 already puts it; it re-opens one pinned relation rather than one lemma plus a parameter condition. (W-3) discards a landed countdown clause and a live margin layer for an obstruction that is local to one coordinate.
